name: Karath Lemongrass-Hibiscus Still
description: An almost-still botanical drink — minimal carbonation, real lemongrass steeped with hibiscus concentrate. Positioned as a wellness-adjacent soda by a small Tier 3 brand that refuses to call itself a wellness brand.
flavor_profile: Clean grassy lemongrass opening, deep tart hibiscus body, very low fizz — drinks more like a cold tea than a soda, with a clean dry finish
slogan: Not a health drink. Just a good one.
cultural_context: Karath has positioned itself as the anti-wellness wellness drink and it works — Tier 3 professionals who are tired of being marketed to respond to the blunt branding. It's common at Tier 3 desk lunches and is quietly gaining traction in Tier 4 casual spaces as a non-alcoholic option at social gatherings.
story_hooks: Karath's founder is being sued by a wellness corponation claiming trademark infringement on the hibiscus-lemongrass flavor combination — a combination that has existed in human cooking for centuries — and the case is becoming a landmark IP dispute
A Tier 4 executive has been ordering Karath in bulk and having it delivered to an address that doesn't appear in any city registry

Someone has been leaving Karath bottles at the scenes of a series of non-violent acts of corporate vandalism across Tier 3 — the bottles are always empty, always upright, always facing the same direction
